n — from the island of Lesbos (as modern reference works give their 
origin), sea-raiders in the eastern Mediterranean before they were anything in the west. 
The chronicle composed within their own circle, the Arabic history of the brothers 
published in French in 1837 as Fondation de la Régence d'Alger, explains their move 
west as a consequence of a quarrel among princes: the Ottoman succession struggle 
between Selim and his brother Korkut left the brothers on the losing side in the Levant 
and in need of a new harbour.

catalogue_leads.context_excerpt: "Comment redécouvrir le monde méditerranéen loin des clichés fabriqués et des images attendues ? Un monde en noir et bleu. Le noir de Goya, des désastres de la guerre, de la mafia et des années noires à Beyrouth, Sarajevo, Alger ou Jérusalem. Le bleu de Miré, celui des Lumières et des poètes, du "Grand Tour" et des villes cosmopolites telles Istanbul ou Alexandrie. Ce livre met en scène tant les représentations que les visions qui composent le rêve méditerranéen un rêve pluriel, restitué à partir des deux rives

catalogue_leads.context_excerpt: eux parties, il donne d'abord à voir 150 oeuvres du XVIIIe siècle à aujourd'hui: peintures, dessins, manuscrits, photographies, installations. Un abécédaire thématique, composé par les meilleurs spécialistes et amoureux de la Méditerranée prolonge ce voyage en près de 50 étapes: A comme Alger en 1830, C comme cosmopolitisme, M comme Marseille en 1943, 0 comme orientalisme... Entre contemplation et analyse, cet ouvrage associe plaisir du texte, originalité des documents et beauté des oeuvres."--P. [4] of cover

catalogue_leads.context_excerpt: Biography of Jan Jansen van Haarlem (c1585-c1640) and his son Anthony Jansen van Salee (1609-c1680). Jan Jansen, a Dutch merchant, became a corsair in Algiers and Sallee (Morocco) before becoming Governor of Oualida, Morocco under Sultan al-Walid. His son Anthony emigrated to New Amsterdam, arriving with his wife Grietje Reyniers, in 1630.
